result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d instill a universal practice of empathy — the habit of truly seeing and valuing every person’s needs, fears and hopes.  

Why empathy?  
• It underpins cooperation. When we recognize another’s pain or aspirations as if they were our own, we’re far more willing to share resources, resolve conflicts peacefully and support one another’s growth.  
• It drives better decisions. Leaders who proactively imagine how policies affect the most vulnerable will design fairer systems of education, health care and social safety nets.  
• It multiplies positive effects. Empathic communities foster mental-wellness, reduce violence and encourage innovation—because people feel safe to take creative risks when they know they’ll be understood and supported.  

How it could look in practice:  
1. Education systems that teach perspective-taking and emotional literacy from early grades.  
2. Workplaces and public services that build in “walk-a-mile” exchanges, where staff literally spend time in clients’ shoes before making policy or budget decisions.  
3. Media and social platforms that reward storytelling and listening over sensationalism and outrage.  

A world where empathy is as routine as reading or arithmetic would still have challenges—but our default response to disagreement would be dialogue instead of division, and cooperation instead of conflict. That one shift in how we relate to one another could unlock solutions to poverty, climate change, healthcare inequities and every other pressing issue.
